title: Endurance

slides.title: NO MAP. NO TENT. SCREWS IN THEIR BOOTS.

slides.text: Shackleton sailed a lifeboat 1,300 km to South Georgia. But they landed on the wrong side of the island.
Shackleton, Worsley and Tom Crean set out across the island's mountains. They pushed screws from the boat into their boot soles for grip.
They walked for about 36 hours without stopping to sleep. In the dark, they coiled a rope, sat on it and slid down a mountainside.
20 May 1916. Three ragged men walk into Stromness whaling station. The men there don't even recognise them.
It took 4 attempts to get through the ice. On 30 August 1916, the Chilean ship Yelcho reached Elephant Island.
Every one of the 22 men waiting there was alive. All 28 men of Endurance survived.
And in 2022, explorers found Endurance 3,008 m (almost 10,000 ft) down, still in one piece.

slides.text: Which true story should we tell next? Comment below and follow for more.

caption: They crossed unmapped mountains with screws in their boots, then went back for their friends. Every one of the 28 men came home. Endurance, the finale.
